sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ pārthivāḥ sarve hṛdayaiḥ samapūjayan na tatra kaś cid vaktuṃ hi vācaṃ prākrāmad agrataḥ
english: All the kings honored that speech with their hearts; no one there stepped forward to utter a word in reply.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasminn abhihite vākye keśavena mahātmanā stimitā hṛṣṭaromāṇa āsan sarve sabhāsadaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When that speech had been delivered by the great-souled Keśava, all the members of the assembly sat still, their body hair bristling with awe.

sanskrit: kaḥ svid uttaram etasmād vaktum utsahate pumān iti sarve manobhis te cintayanti sma pārthivāḥ
english: "Who indeed among men would dare to speak in answer to this?" — so all the kings reflected in their minds.

sanskrit: tathā teṣu ca sarveṣu tūṣṇīṃbhūteṣu rājasu jāmadagnya idaṃ vākyam abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: And while all those kings sat thus in silence, the son of Jamadagni spoke these words in the assembly of the Kurus.

sanskrit: imām ekopamāṃ rājañ śṛṇu satyām aśaṅkitaḥ tāṃ śrutvā śreya ādatsva yadi sādhv iti manyase
english: "Hear this one parable, O king — it is true, so receive it without doubt; having heard it, adopt the better course, if you consider it sound."

sanskrit: rājā dambhodbhavo nāma sārvabhaumaḥ purābhavat akhilāṃ bubhuje sarvāṃ pṛthivīm iti naḥ śrutam
english: "There was in former times a king named Dambhodbhava, sovereign of the whole earth; he enjoyed dominion over all the land entire — so we have heard."

sanskrit: sa sma nityaṃ niśāpāye prātar utthāya vīryavān brāhmaṇān kṣatriyāṃś caiva pṛcchann āste mahārathaḥ
english: "That mighty warrior, rising each morning at the end of night, would sit and question the Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas alike."

sanskrit: asti kaś cid viśiṣṭo vā madvidho vā bhaved yudhi śūdro vaiśyaḥ kṣatriyo vā brāhmaṇo vāpi śastrabhṛt
english: "'Is there anyone superior to me, or even my equal in battle — whether a Śūdra, a Vaiśya, a Kṣatriya, or even a Brāhmaṇa bearing arms?'"

sanskrit: iti bruvann anvacarat sa rājā pṛthivīm imām darpeṇa mahatā mattaḥ kaṃ cid anyam acintayan
english: "Saying this, that king roamed across the earth, intoxicated with great pride, giving no thought to anyone else."

sanskrit: taṃ sma vaidyā akṛpaṇā brāhmaṇāḥ sarvato 'bhayāḥ pratyaṣedhanta rājānaṃ ślāghamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Brāhmaṇas who were wise and fearless on all sides repeatedly tried to restrain that king as he boasted again and again."

sanskrit: pratiṣidhyamāno 'py asakṛt pṛcchaty eva sa vai dvijān abhimānī śriyā mattas tam ūcur brāhmaṇās tadā
english: "Though restrained, he kept asking the twice-born more than once, arrogant and intoxicated by his prosperity; and then the Brāhmaṇas spoke to him thus."

sanskrit: tapasvino mahātmāno vedavratasamanvitāḥ udīryamāṇaṃ rājānaṃ krodhadīptā dvijātayaḥ
english: "Those ascetics, great-souled and endowed with the vows of the Vedas, the twice-born, blazing with anger at the king who kept boasting —"

sanskrit: anekajananaṃ sakhyaṃ yayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ tayos tvaṃ na samo rājan bhavitāsi kadā cana
english: "'There are two lion-like men whose friendship spans many births; to them, O king, you shall never be equal — not ever.'"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājā tu punaḥ papraccha tān dvijān kva tau vīrau kvajanmānau kiṃkarmāṇau ca kau ca tau
english: "So spoken to, the king again asked those twice-born: 'Where are those two heroes? Where were they born? What are their deeds? Who are they?'"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ naro nārāyaṇaś caiva tāpasāv iti naḥ śrutam āyātau mānuṣe loke tābhyāṃ yudhyasva pārthiva
english: "The Brāhmaṇas said: 'Nara and Nārāyaṇa — they are ascetics, so we have heard; they have descended into the world of men. Go and fight with them, O king.'"

sanskrit: śrūyate tau mahātmānau naranārāyaṇāv ubhau tapo ghoram anirdeśyaṃ tapyete gandhamādane
english: "'It is said that those two great-souled ones, both Nara and Nārāyaṇa, are practicing dreadful and indescribable austerities on Mount Gandhamādana.'"

sanskrit: rāma uvāca sa rājā mahatīṃ senāṃ yojayitvā ṣaḍaṅginīm amṛṣyamāṇaḥ saṃprāyād yatra tāv aparājitau
english: Rāma said: "That king, unable to bear this, mustered a great army with its six divisions and marched to where those two unconquered ones dwelt."

sanskrit: sa gatvā viṣamaṃ ghoraṃ parvataṃ gandhamādanam mṛgayāṇo 'nvagacchat tau tāpasāv aparājitau
english: "Reaching that rugged and terrible mountain Gandhamādana, he followed in search of those two unconquered ascetics."

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā kṣutpipāsābhyāṃ kṛśau dhamanisaṃtatau śītavātātapaiś caiva karśitau puruṣottamau abhigamyopasaṃgṛhya paryapṛcchad anāmayam
english: "Seeing those two foremost of men, emaciated by hunger and thirst, their veins prominent, worn thin by cold wind and sun, he approached, greeted them, and inquired after their well-being."

sanskrit: tam arcitvā mūlaphalair āsanenodakena ca nyamantrayetāṃ rājānaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ kriyatām iti
english: "Honouring him with roots, fruits, a seat, and water, the two invited the king, asking: 'What is to be done? What service may we render?'"

sanskrit: dambhodbhava uvāca bāhubhyāṃ me jitā bhūmir nihatāḥ sarvaśatravaḥ bhavadbhyāṃ yuddham ākāṅkṣann upayāto 'smi parvatam ātithyaṃ dīyatām etat kāṅkṣitaṃ me ciraṃ prati
english: "Dambhodbhava said: 'I have conquered the earth with my own arms and slain all my enemies; I have come to this mountain seeking battle with you two. Grant me this hospitality — it is what I have long desired.'"

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇāv ūcatuḥ apetakrodhalobho 'yam āśramo rājasattama na hy asminn āśrame yuddhaṃ kutaḥ śastraṃ kuto 'nṛjuḥ anyatra yuddham ākāṅkṣva bahavaḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣitau
english: "Nara and Nārāyaṇa said: 'This hermitage is free of anger and greed, O best of kings; in this hermitage there is no room for battle, no room for weapons, no room for falsehood. Seek battle elsewhere — there are many Kṣatriyas on earth.'"

sanskrit: rāma uvāca ucyamānas tathāpi sma bhūya evābhyabhāṣata punaḥ punaḥ kṣamyamāṇaḥ sāntvyamānaś ca bhārata dambhodbhavo yuddham icchann āhvayaty eva tāpasau
english: "Rāma said: Though spoken to thus, and though forgiven and soothed again and again, O Bharata, Dambhodbhava, intent on battle, challenged the two ascetics once more."

sanskrit: tato naras tv iṣīkāṇāṃ muṣṭim ādāya kaurava abravīd ehi yudhyasva yuddhakāmuka kṣatriya
english: "Then Nara, taking up a handful of grass-stalks, O Kaurava, said: 'Come then and fight, O Kṣatriya who craves battle!'"

sanskrit: sarvaśastrāṇi cādatsva yojayasva ca vāhinīm ahaṃ hi te vineṣyāmi yuddhaśraddhām itaḥ param
english: "'Take up all your weapons and array your army; I shall rid you of your faith in battle from this day forward.'"

sanskrit: dambhodbhava uvāca yady etad astram asmāsu yuktaṃ tāpasa manyase etenāpi tvayā yotsye yuddhārthī hy aham āgataḥ
english: "Dambhodbhava said: 'If you think this weapon fit to use against us, O ascetic, I will fight with even this; I have come here for battle.'"

sanskrit: rāma uvāca ity uktvā śaravarṣeṇa sarvataḥ samavākirat dambhodbhavas tāpasaṃ taṃ jighāṃsuḥ sahasainikaḥ
english: "Rāma said: Having spoken thus, Dambhodbhava, wishing to slay the ascetic, showered arrows from every side upon him together with his army."

sanskrit: tasya tān asyato ghorān iṣūn paratanucchidaḥ kadarthīkṛtya sa munir iṣīkābhir apānudat
english: "As he let fly those dreadful arrows that could pierce an enemy's body, the sage made them of no account and warded them off with his grass-stalks."

sanskrit: tato 'smai prāsṛjad ghoram aiṣīkam aparājitaḥ astram apratisaṃdheyaṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: "Then the unconquered one released against him a dreadful grass-stalk weapon, a weapon beyond all counter-measure — and it seemed like a wonder."

sanskrit: teṣām akṣīṇi karṇāṃś ca nastakāṃś caiva māyayā nimittavedhī sa munir iṣīkābhiḥ samarpayat
english: "That sage, striking at vital points by his power of illusion, pierced their eyes, their ears, and their nostrils with his grass-stalks."

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā śvetam ākāśam iṣīkābhiḥ samācitam pādayor nyapatad rājā svasti me 'stv iti cābravīt
english: "Seeing the sky turned white and filled with grass-stalks, the king fell at Nara's feet and cried: 'Let me be spared!'"

sanskrit: tam abravīn naro rājañ śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇaiṣiṇām brahmaṇyo bhava dharmātmā mā ca smaivaṃ punaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Nara said to him: 'O king, one who seeks refuge must be granted refuge. Be devoted to the Brāhmaṇas and righteous in spirit; and do not ever act in this way again.'"

sanskrit: mā ca darpasamāviṣṭaḥ kṣepsīḥ kāṃś cit kadā cana alpīyāṃsaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ vā tat te rājan paraṃ hitam
english: "'And do not, seized by arrogance, ever despise anyone, whether lesser or greater — that, O king, is your supreme good.'"

sanskrit: kṛtaprajño vītalobho nirahaṃkāra ātmavān dāntaḥ kṣānto mṛduḥ kṣemaḥ prajāḥ pālaya pārthiva
english: "'Possessed of discernment, free from greed, without ego, self-controlled, tamed, patient, gentle, and peaceful — thus protect your subjects, O king.'"

sanskrit: anujñātaḥ svasti gaccha maivaṃ bhūyaḥ samācareḥ kuśalaṃ brāhmaṇān pṛccher āvayor vacanād bhṛśam
english: "'You are dismissed — go in peace, and do not act in this manner again. Pay heed to the well-being of the Brāhmaṇas, as we earnestly command you.'"

sanskrit: tato rājā tayoḥ pādāv abhivādya mahātmanoḥ pratyājagāma svapuraṃ dharmaṃ caivācinod bhṛśam
english: "Then the king, having bowed at the feet of those two great-souled ones, returned to his own city, and he earnestly cultivated righteousness."

sanskrit: sumahac cāpi tat karma yan nareṇa kṛtaṃ purā tato guṇaiḥ subahubhiḥ śreṣṭho nārāyaṇo 'bhavat
english: "That deed which Nara performed in former times was also very great; and by virtue of his many qualities, Nārāyaṇa became the most excellent of all."

sanskrit: tasmād yāvad dhanuḥśreṣṭhe gāṇḍīve 'straṃ na yujyate tāvat tvaṃ mānam utsṛjya gaccha rājan dhanaṃjayam
english: "Therefore, before weapons are fitted to the bow Gāṇḍīva, that best of bows, go to Dhanañjaya, O king, laying aside your pride."

sanskrit: kākudīkaṃ śukaṃ nākam akṣisaṃtarjanaṃ tathā saṃtānaṃ nartanaṃ ghoram āsyamodakam aṣṭamam
english: "The kakudika, the shuka, the naka, the eye-terrorizer — the santana, the nartana the dreadful, and the asyamodaka — these are eight."

sanskrit: etair viddhāḥ sarva eva maraṇaṃ yānti mānavāḥ unmattāś ca viceṣṭante naṣṭasaṃjñā vicetasaḥ
english: "Struck by these, all men go to their death; they writhe about maddened, their consciousness and wits destroyed."

sanskrit: svapante ca plavante ca chardayanti ca mānavāḥ mūtrayante ca satataṃ rudanti ca hasanti ca
english: "Men struck by them fall asleep, leap about, vomit, discharge urine continually, weep, and laugh uncontrollably."

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyā guṇāḥ pārthe tadviśiṣṭo janārdanaḥ tvam eva bhūyo jānāsi kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: "The virtues of Pārtha are beyond counting, and Janārdana surpasses even him. You yourself know Dhanañjaya, the son of Kuntī, better than I."

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau yau tau tāv evārjunakeśavau vijānīhi mahārāja pravīrau puruṣarṣabhau
english: "Know, O great king, that those two — Nara and Nārāyaṇa — are none other than Arjuna and Keśava, those two foremost heroes, those two bulls among men."

sanskrit: yady etad evaṃ jānāsi na ca mām atiśaṅkase āryāṃ matiṃ samāsthāya śāmya bhārata pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: "If you know this to be true and do not greatly distrust me, then, taking recourse to a noble resolve, make peace with the Pāṇḍavas, O Bharata."

sanskrit: atha cen manyase śreyo na me bhedo bhaved iti praśāmya bharataśreṣṭha mā ca yuddhe manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Or if you consider it best that there be no breach between us, then, O best of the Bharatas, make peace and do not set your mind on war."

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ ca kuruśreṣṭha kulaṃ bahumataṃ bhuvi tat tathaivāstu bhadraṃ te svārtham evānucintaya
english: "Your family, O best of the Kurus, is highly esteemed on earth — let it remain so. May you fare well; consider your own true interest."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jāmadagnyavacaḥ śrutvā kaṇvo 'pi bhagavān ṛṣiḥ duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Jamadagni's son, the venerable sage Kanva also spoke these words to Duryodhana in the assembly of the Kurus.

sanskrit: akṣayaś cāvyayaś caiva brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ tathaiva bhagavantau tau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: "Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, is imperishable and immutable; and likewise those two lordly sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa are the same."

sanskrit: ādityānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ viṣṇur ekaḥ sanātanaḥ ajayyaś cāvyayaś caiva śāśvataḥ prabhur īśvaraḥ
english: "Among all the Ādityas, Viṣṇu alone is eternal, unconquerable, immutable, everlasting, the lord and sovereign."

sanskrit: nimittamaraṇās tv anye candrasūryau mahī jalam vāyur agnis tathākāśaṃ grahās tārāgaṇās tathā
english: "Others die when their occasion comes — the moon and sun, the earth and water, wind and fire and space, the planets, and the multitudes of stars."

sanskrit: te ca kṣayānte jagato hitvā lokatrayaṃ sadā kṣayaṃ gacchanti vai sarve sṛjyante ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: "At the dissolution of the universe they all perish, abandoning the three worlds forever, and they are created again and again."

sanskrit: muhūrtamaraṇās tv anye mānuṣā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ tiryagyonyaś ca ye cānye jīvalokacarāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: "Others die in but a moment — humans, beasts and birds, and those born in animal wombs, and whatever other creatures are known to roam the world of living beings."

sanskrit: bhūyiṣṭhena tu rājānaḥ śriyaṃ bhuktvāyuṣaḥ kṣaye maraṇaṃ pratigacchanti bhoktuṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛtam
english: "Kings for the most part, after enjoying prosperity, go to their death at the end of their allotted life, to reap the fruits of their good and evil deeds."

sanskrit: sa bhavān dharmaputreṇa śamaṃ kartum ihārhati pāṇḍavāḥ kuravaś caiva pālayantu vasuṃdharām
english: "You, sir, should make peace with the son of Dharma here and now; let the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus together protect the earth."

sanskrit: balavān aham ity eva na mantavyaṃ suyodhana balavanto hi balibhir dṛśyante puruṣarṣabha
english: "Do not think only 'I am strong,' O Suyodhana; the powerful are measured against the powerful, O bull among men."

sanskrit: na balaṃ balināṃ madhye balaṃ bhavati kaurava balavanto hi te sarve pāṇḍavā devavikramāḥ
english: "Strength is not strength in the midst of the strong, O Kaurava; all those Pāṇḍavas are strong, their valor equal to that of the gods."

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam mātaler dātukāmasya kanyāṃ mṛgayato varam
english: "In this connection they also cite this ancient tale — of Matali, who wished to give away his daughter and was searching for a bridegroom."

sanskrit: matas trailokyarājasya mātalir nāma sārathiḥ tasyaikaiva kule kanyā rūpato lokaviśrutā
english: "Matali was the name of the charioteer of the king of the three worlds; he had a single daughter in his family, renowned throughout the world for her beauty."

sanskrit: guṇakeśīti vikhyātā nāmnā sā devarūpiṇī śriyā ca vapuṣā caiva striyo 'nyāḥ sātiricyate
english: "She was famed by the name Guṇakeśī, divine in her form, surpassing all other women in beauty and in bodily grace."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pradānasamayaṃ mātaliḥ saha bhāryayā jñātvā vimamṛśe rājaṃs tatparaḥ paricintayan
english: "When Matali and his wife perceived that the time for her marriage had come, O king, he fell into deep reflection, pondering with full attention."

sanskrit: dhik khalv alaghuśīlānām ucchritānāṃ yaśasvinām narāṇām ṛddhasattvānāṃ kule kanyāprarohaṇam
english: "'How lamentable it is indeed that a daughter is born into the family of men who are of lofty character, exalted station, fame, and abundant virtue."

sanskrit: mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra caiva pradīyate kulatrayaṃ saṃśayitaṃ kurute kanyakā satām
english: "'A noble daughter puts three families in jeopardy — her mother's family, her father's family, and the family into which she is given.'"

sanskrit: devamānuṣalokau dvau mānasenaiva cakṣuṣā avagāhyaiva vicitau na ca me rocate varaḥ
english: "'I have searched through both the world of gods and the world of men with the eye of my mind alone, and yet no bridegroom pleases me.'"

sanskrit: na devān naiva ditijān na gandharvān na mānuṣān arocayaṃ varakṛte tathaiva bahulān ṛṣīn
english: "'Neither the gods, nor the sons of Diti, nor the Gandharvas, nor humans — not these, nor the many sages — did any please me as a worthy match.'"

sanskrit: bhāryayā tu sa saṃmantrya saha rātrau sudharmayā mātalir nāgalokāya cakāra gamane matim
english: "Then, having consulted at night with his wife Sudharma, Matali resolved to journey to the realm of the Nāgas."

sanskrit: na me devamanuṣyeṣu guṇakeśyāḥ samo varaḥ rūpato dṛśyate kaś cin nāgeṣu bhavitā dhruvam
english: "'Among gods and men I see no bridegroom worthy of Guṇakeśī; such a one will surely be found among the Nāgas.'"

sanskrit: ity āmantrya sudharmāṃ sa kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam kanyāṃ śirasy upāghrāya praviveśa mahītalam
english: "Having thus taken leave of Sudharma and circumambulating her, he smelled the head of his daughter in farewell and entered the depths of the earth."

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca mātalis tu vrajan mārge nāradena maharṣiṇā varuṇaṃ gacchatā draṣṭuṃ samāgacchad yadṛcchayā
english: Kanva said: "Now, as Matali was traveling, he chanced to meet on the road the great sage Nārada, who was himself going to see Varuṇa."

sanskrit: nārado 'thābravīd enaṃ kva bhavān gantum udyataḥ svena vā sūta kāryeṇa śāsanād vā śatakratoḥ
english: "And Nārada said to him: 'Where are you bound, sir? Is it on your own business, or on the command of Śatakratu?'"

sanskrit: mātalir nāradenaivaṃ saṃpṛṣṭaḥ pathi gacchatā yathāvat sarvam ācaṣṭa svakāryaṃ varuṇaṃ prati
english: "Matali, thus questioned by Nārada as they traveled the road, recounted everything exactly as it was — his own business and his errand toward Varuṇa's realm."

sanskrit: tam uvācātha sa munir gacchāvaḥ sahitāv iti salileśadidṛkṣārtham aham apy udyato divaḥ
english: "Then the sage said to him: 'Let us go together; I too have set forth from heaven, wishing to see the lord of the waters.'"

sanskrit: ahaṃ te sarvam ākhyāsye darśayan vasudhātalam dṛṣṭvā tatra varaṃ kaṃ cid rocayiṣyāva mātale
english: "'I shall show you all, revealing the depths of the earth, and having looked there together, perhaps we shall find some bridegroom who pleases us, O Matali.'"

sanskrit: avagāhya tato bhūmim ubhau mātalināradau dadṛśāte mahātmānau lokapālam apāṃ patim
english: "Then plunging into the earth, both Matali and Nārada, those two great-souled ones, beheld the guardian of the world, the lord of the waters."

sanskrit: tatra devarṣisadṛśīṃ pūjāṃ prāpa sa nāradaḥ mahendrasadṛśīṃ caiva mātaliḥ pratyapadyata
english: "There Nārada received worship befitting a divine sage, and Matali in turn was honored with worship befitting the great Indra himself."

sanskrit: tāv ubhau prītamanasau kāryavattāṃ nivedya ha varuṇenābhyanujñātau nāgalokaṃ viceratuḥ
english: "Those two, their hearts gladdened, declared the purpose of their visit, and having been given leave by Varuṇa, they roamed about the realm of the Nāgas."

sanskrit: nāradaḥ sarvabhūtānām antarbhūminivāsinām jānaṃś cakāra vyākhyānaṃ yantuḥ sarvam aśeṣataḥ
english: "Nārada, knowing all the creatures who dwell within the earth, explained everything to him who was going — leaving nothing out."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca dṛṣṭas te varuṇas tāta putrapautrasamāvṛtaḥ paśyodakapateḥ sthānaṃ sarvatobhadram ṛddhimat
english: "Nārada said: 'Varuṇa has been seen by you, dear friend, surrounded by his sons and grandsons; now look upon the abode of the lord of the waters — auspicious on all sides and full of riches.'"

sanskrit: eṣa putro mahāprājño varuṇasyeha gopateḥ eṣa taṃ śīlavṛttena śaucena ca viśiṣyate
english: "'This is the greatly wise son of Varuṇa, the lord of cattle here; this one excels even him in nobility of character, conduct, and purity.'"

sanskrit: eṣo 'sya putro 'bhimataḥ puṣkaraḥ puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ rūpavān darśanīyaś ca somaputryā vṛtaḥ patiḥ
english: "'This is his beloved son Puṣkara, lotus-eyed, handsome and fair to look upon — he has been chosen as husband by the daughter of Soma.'"

sanskrit: jyotsnākālīti yām āhur dvitīyāṃ rūpataḥ śriyam ādityasyaiva goḥ putro jyeṣṭhaḥ putraḥ kṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: "'She whom they call Jyotsnakali, a second beauty of form — she is the eldest daughter, born of the sun's own celestial cow, so it is said.'"
